subject: Computer Networking
title: Mosaic: The Browser That Changed Everything
description: Learn Mosaic: The Browser That Changed Everything in one minute.

hook.text: The web existed for two years before most people saw it. Mosaic made it visual, clickable, and accessible.

buildup.text: Released in 1993 by NCSA, Mosaic displayed images inline with text. Previous browsers were text-only.

discovery.text: It ran on Windows, Mac, and Unix. Anyone with a PC and a modem could browse the web for the first time.

twist.text: Mosaic's lead developer, Marc Andreessen, left to co-found Netscape — launching the dot-com era.

climax.text: In one year, web traffic jumped from 1% to 20% of internet backbone traffic. Mosaic was the catalyst.

punchline.text: Mosaic showed the world what the web could look like.

quiz.question: What was revolutionary about the Mosaic browser?
options: It displayed images inline with text on multiple platforms
It was the first browser to use HTTPS

details.summary: Mosaic, released in 1993 by Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina at NCSA, was the first graphical web browser to display images inline with text. It made the web visual, intuitive, and accessible to ordinary people, triggering the explosive growth of the World Wide Web.
details.whyItMatters: Mosaic turned the web from a text-only research tool into a visual medium. It was the spark that ignited mainstream internet adoption and the entire web industry.
takeaways: Mosaic displayed images inline with text for the first time
It made the web accessible to non-technical users
Mosaic's team went on to create Netscape Navigator

faq.question: Why was inline image display so revolutionary?
faq.answer: Previous browsers displayed text only, with images opening in separate windows. Mosaic rendered images alongside text, creating visual web pages. This made the web look like a magazine rather than a terminal. Visual presentation made the web compelling to millions of people.

faq.question: How did Mosaic lead to Netscape?
faq.answer: Marc Andreessen left NCSA and co-founded Netscape Communications with Jim Clark. Netscape Navigator improved on Mosaic and became the dominant browser. Netscape's IPO in 1995 marked the beginning of the dot-com era and browser-based internet commerce.
